title: The Day the Dinosaurs Vanished
paragraphs: About sixty-six million years ago, the last of the non-bird dinosaurs disappeared from Earth. For decades, scientists argued about the cause, proposing everything from volcanic eruptions to changes in climate. The theory that has gained the most support blames a huge asteroid that struck what is now the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico.

The impact would have thrown enormous amounts of dust and debris into the atmosphere. Sunlight would have been blocked, plants would have struggled, and the food chains that depended on them would have begun to collapse. The Natural History Museum in London points out that dinosaurs were already living in a changing world, since some environmental changes had begun millions of years earlier. In that view, the asteroid was the final blow rather than the only cause.

Not everything died, however. Birds are the living descendants of one group of dinosaurs, and their ancestors survived the catastrophe. So, the extinction was an ending for some lineages, but a beginning for others, including the mammals that eventually gave rise to humans. Without that disaster, the world we know today might look very different.
